title: land pushes an auto-merging code merge request before the item's own checks run
goal: On the code lane, backlog.py land runs the item's checks (and a bug's repro) before sync --push opens the auto-merging code/<id> request, stopping at step checks when one fails; a TestBacklogLand test plants a failing check on a code item and asserts nothing was pushed

run: import pathlib,sys; s=pathlib.Path('_tools/bl_land.py').read_text(encoding='utf-8'); b=s[s.index('def cmd_land'):]; b=b[:b.index(chr(10)+'def ',1)]; sys.exit(0 if 'land_checks(' in b else 1)

repro_reason: the fix changes which value the code reads, and showing the defect needs a planted scenario that is this item's own test, still to be written; no cheaper command runs the behaviour, so the repro reads the source until that test exists
notes: Retro of SP-w3xmbdra: a check whose pytest selection runs zero tests (exit 5, a malformed perfcheck.py time form in ST-ykvho3zp and ST-5q5b5qtz) passed review of the plan and failed only at land; the land-time run of the item's checks should name a zero-test selection as a malformed check, and a planner runs each check once before a sprint commits the item. Retro of BG-qks4ikyr: a repro naming a concrete item id (BG-3i46pccw) rots once that item closes, so done would fail for its own reason; backlog check could warn on an item id in a repro or check argv.
